passages.text: Now King Xerxes imposed tribute throughout the land, even to its farthest shores.
passages.sermon: King Xerxes ruled a vast kingdom.\r\nHe imposed a tax on the land.\r\nHe also imposed a tax on the distant islands.
passages.original: וַיָּשֶׂם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אֲחָשֵׁרֹשׁ מַ֛ס עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ וְאִיֵּ֥י הַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: And all of Mordecai’s powerful and magnificent accomplishments, together with the full account of the greatness to which the king had raised him, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia?
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
The king made Mordecai great.
Mordecai did powerful things.
Mordecai did magnificent things.
The king raised Mordecai to greatness.
Writers recorded all of Mordecai’s deeds.
Writers recorded the full account of Mordecai’s greatness.
They wrote these things in the Book of the Chronicles.
This book belongs to the kings of Media and Persia.
passages.original: וְכָל־ מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה תָקְפּוֹ֙ וּגְב֣וּרָת֔וֹ וּפָרָשַׁת֙ גְּדֻלַּ֣ת מָרְדֳּכַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר גִּדְּל֖וֹ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ הֲלוֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֙פֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י הַיָּמִ֔ים לְמַלְכֵ֖י מָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃

passages.text: For Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Xerxes, preeminent among the Jews and highly favored by his many kinsmen, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his countrymen.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai served as second in command to King Xerxes.
Mordecai was important among the Jews.
Many of his fellow Jews favored Mordecai.
Mordecai sought the good of his people.
Mordecai spoke peace to all his descendants.
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ מָרְדֳּכַ֣י הַיְּהוּדִ֗י מִשְׁנֶה֙ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ וְגָדוֹל֙ לַיְּהוּדִ֔ים וְרָצ֖וּי לְרֹ֣ב אֶחָ֑יו דֹּרֵ֥שׁ טוֹב֙ לְעַמּ֔וֹ וְדֹבֵ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל־ זַרְעֽוֹ׃
